# FDG5118

> DO NOT use params arrays if the array is modified by the member taking the params array parameter.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.8.4 Members with Variable Number of Parameters.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG5118
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Do not use params for the parameter '{0}' of '{1}', which modifies the array

FDG5118 reports the params array parameter of an externally visible method or constructor when its body, lambdas and local functions included, assigns an element of the array: a simple, compound, null-coalescing or deconstruction assignment, or an increment or decrement. Overrides and interface implementations are not reported. Changes made through calls, such as Array.Sort or Array.Clear, or through ref arguments, are not seen, and neither are params collections other than arrays (C# 13). The text asks not to use params for such a member, so the fix removes params, which callers that pass the elements inline rely on; it is breaking, and there is no code fix.

## From the book

Because many compilers turn the arguments to the member into a temporary array at the call site, the array might be a temporary object, and therefore any modifications to the array will be lost.
